1.explanation:
• DangerButton.js: this file defines the built-in <DangerButton> wrapper; it needs to render a visually hidden span (with a unique id) and add an aria-describedby prop to the button so screen readers announce “Danger!” automatically.  
• DangerButton-test.js: the unit tests for DangerButton must be updated (or new tests added) to verify that the aria-describedBy attribute and hidden span are rendered correctly.  
• Button.js: the underlying <Button> component must be capable of accepting and forwarding the aria-describedby attribute (and any extra props) to the native <button> element; if it currently filters out unknown ARIA props it must be updated.  
• Button.mdx: the documentation for the Button component should include guidance and code examples for the danger variant’s ARIA support (showing the hidden span and aria-describedBy usage) so that consumers know the correct pattern.
1.bug_scenario: The Carbon “danger” button variants (primary, tertiary, and ghost) only convey their destructive status visually (red styling and border) but don’t announce that danger to screen‐reader users. The repro code shows manually adding an aria‐describedBy reference to a visually hidden “Danger!” span inside a custom DangerButton wrapper—and in the screenshot of the actual rendered HTML you can see the aria‐describedBy on the button and the hidden span—but the built-in Carbon DangerButton component doesn’t ship with that markup out of the box. As a result, screen–reader users will only hear “button” or the button label, but not “danger” or “destructive action.”
